title: Shahid Kapoor Has Two Projects Left. After That, He Has No Idea What He's Doing. That's the Point.
excerpt: In a revealing interview, the Cocktail 2 star says Bollywood broke its own writers — and he'd rather wait for the right script than fake busy.
body:
There's a version of **Shahid Kapoor** that doesn't exist anymore — the one who said yes to everything, who juggled four films a year, who chased box office weekends the way everyone around him did. That version is gone. In its place is a 45-year-old actor who just told *The Hollywood Reporter India*, with zero panic in his voice: "I don't know what I'm going to do after that."

"After that" is two projects. Just two. **Cocktail 2**, the buzzy romantic dramedy opening June 19 with **Kriti Sanon** and **Rashmika Mandanna**, and **Farzi Season 2**, the Prime Video crime thriller that's 60 per cent done shooting and wrapping by September. After those, Shahid Kapoor's calendar is wide open — and he wants it that way.

> "I don't want to disappoint the audience. What hurts me the most is when they walk out of the theater unsatisfied." — Shahid Kapoor

In a moment where every other A-lister is frantically locking franchise sequels and spy universe installments, Shahid's stillness feels almost radical. IMDb has nine upcoming titles attached to his name — *Karna*, *Ashwatthama — The Saga Continues*, and several others. He laughed that off with the kind of confidence only genuine box office credibility gives you: "If the IMDb team wants to know what my upcoming projects are, they could call me."



> **"In its place is a 45-year-old actor who just told *The Hollywood Reporter India*, with zero panic in his voice: "I don't know what I'm going to do after that."

"After that" is two projects."**


## The Farzi Update Diaspora Fans Have Been Waiting For

For NRI audiences who devoured the first season of **Farzi** — and there were millions of you, making it Prime Video India's most-watched debut — the update is substantial. Shooting for Season 2 kicked off in March with Shahid sharing monochrome behind-the-scenes glimpses from set. As of this week, he confirms 60 per cent of production is complete, with the remaining shoot expected to wrap by September 2026.

The show that turned a counterfeiting hustle into one of Indian OTT's sharpest character studies is coming back with even higher stakes. Based on Shahid's own enthusiasm, it sounds like Raj & DK — the creators behind *The Family Man* and *Citadel India* — have given Sunny an even darker, more complex arc. "Whatever they have taken me through sounds like a level up from the first season," Shahid said at an earlier Prime Video event, "but it also feels very much like a natural progression of the story."

**Vijay Sethupathi** returns as the relentless task force officer Michael. **Raashii Khanna** is back as RBI officer Megha. **Kay Kay Menon** remains the cunning Mansoor Dalal. The gang's all here — and with Shahid reportedly earning ₹40 crore for the second season, his biggest pay cheque ever, the stakes match the salary.

## On Bollywood's Script Crisis

But it's Shahid's diagnosis of the industry's deeper problem that cuts sharpest. When asked about the frequently repeated complaint that Bollywood is running out of good scripts, he didn't deflect. He went surgical.

> "We always want to talk about the problem, we don't want to go to the root of it. To me, it came because we went through a phase where we were only making remakes and franchise movies, and I'm sure there were writers sitting out there with good content who got tired and just left." — Shahid Kapoor

It's the kind of thing plenty of people in the industry think privately but rarely say on record. The franchise machine — Spy Universes, horror sequels, comedy-franchise installments — has consumed Bollywood's release calendar so thoroughly that original voices have been sidelined. Shahid isn't exempt from the system (Cocktail 2 is, after all, a sequel), but his willingness to call it out while inside it is the rare honest moment.

He went further: the industry didn't respect its writers enough to keep them. Social media killed the patience required for slow-burn storytelling. And now, the talent pipeline is thinner than anyone will admit publicly.

## What This Means for the Diaspora

If you're watching from the US, UK, or Canada, Shahid Kapoor's next few months look like this: **Cocktail 2** in theaters June 19, which you should have no trouble finding screens for — it's the most anticipated Hindi film of the month, topping IMDb's most-wanted list with a 21 per cent page view share. And **Farzi Season 2** on Prime Video, likely late 2026 or early 2027, dropping directly onto your streaming queue wherever you are.

After that? Nothing. And that might be exactly what Bollywood needs more of — actors who'd rather do nothing than do something forgettable.
